title: Every Entry Is In My Handwriting

scenes.narration: Every entry in the lost property log this week is in my handwriting. I did not write any of them.
scenes.imagePrompt: Close-up of ledger pages filled with handwriting in faded ink, too small to read, one page edge curling under lamplight, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: I lock up at six. In the morning there are things on the counter, already tagged, already written in.
scenes.imagePrompt: A wooden counter in a dim basement office with a scarf, a single glove and a set of keys lying on it, each tied to a brown luggage tag, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: The handed in by column says the same every time. Night staff. Nobody works in this building at night.
scenes.imagePrompt: An empty office building stairwell at night, emergency lighting, a basement door at the bottom of the stairs standing half open, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.subtext: The way I wrote when I started.
scenes.narration: It is my handwriting, but neater. The way I wrote when I started here, nine years ago.
scenes.imagePrompt: An old fountain pen and a brass nib tin on a worn desk blotter covered in faint ink marks, lit by a single bulb, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain
